functions.name: readSkeletonData_skinsCreateAttachment
functions.address_range: 0x28c7a4-0x28c7e4 (blocks #1 minus the path stub) + the 0x28cc68 convergence it branches to
functions.semantics: loader = json->loader; attachment = spAttachmentLoader_createAttachment(loader, skin, type, name, path) with the fifth argument on the stack (0x28c7ac str r5,[sp]); NULL -> block #5/#6; else stored = ((int32_t*)attachment)[1] and an unsigned compare against 4 selects the jump-table landing (region parser / bbox parser / mesh parser for 2 and 3 / path parser), then spSkin_addAttachment(skin, slotIndex, name, attachment) at 0x28cc68.
instruction_anchors: 0x28c7c0 ldr r3,[r6,#4] (the type STORED IN THE OBJECT)
quirks: the jump table switches on the type the LOADER stored at +0x04, never on the requested type; a loader may answer a linkedmesh request with an object whose +0x04 is 2 and the mesh parser then runs
`addls` is an unsigned test: a stored type of 5 or 0xffffffff takes the 0x28c7cc fall-through, so the attachment is added without a field parse
table entries 2 and 3 point at the same mesh parser (0x28cb20); its 1/0 return is discarded exactly like 0x28cb1c b 0x28cc68, so a mesh queued for the linkedmesh postpass is still added to the skin

functions.name: readSkeletonData_skinsLoaderErrorTail
functions.semantics: data = [sp,#0x34]; spSkeletonData_dispose(data) FIRST; then _spSkeletonJson_setError(json, root, loader->error1, loader->error2) with the pair loaded by 0x28cf90 ldm r3,{r2,r3}; returns the failed attachment (r6, 0).
instruction_anchors: 0x28cfa0/0x28cfa4 mov r2,#1 ; b 0x28c7a4 (the boundingbox stub in the same window)
quirks: the message is not static text: it is loader->error1 (+0x00) and the argument is loader->error2 (+0x04)
the 0x28bdcc epilogue and the root ownership stay outside this module (census §5.3 / §3.3)

functions.name: readSkeletonData_skinsAttachmentAdd
functions.semantics: spSkin_addAttachment(skin (r9), slotIndex ([sp,#0x28]), name (r7), attachment (r6)) through the REAL c/spine_skin body at 0x28ecd8.
quirks: the name handed to the skin is r7 = attachmentMap->name (+0x1c) loaded at 0x28c6e8, i.e. the JSON MEMBER KEY, while createAttachment receives r6 = Json_getString(map,"name",key); the two differ whenever a map carries a "name" property
c/spine_skin copies the name into the entry (line 38), so the borrowed Json string is not retained

functions.name: readSkeletonData_skinsAdvance
functions.semantics: attachment = attachment->next; if non-NULL -> ATTACHMENT back edge 0x28c6e8. Otherwise slot = slot->next; if non-NULL -> SLOT back edge 0x28c6c4. Otherwise skin = skin->next; if non-NULL -> SKIN back edge 0x28c664, else DONE.
quirks: the two stack cells [sp,#0x1c] and [sp,#0x18] hold the current Json node and are advanced by reading +0x00, so modelling them as cursor fields is exact
0x28cc9c ldr r11,[sp,#0x34] and 0x28ccb4 mov r9,r11 are chain-level data restores (census §5.3) and are NOT re-emitted here

functions.name: readSkeletonData_skinsAttachmentLevel
functions.address_range: 0x28cc7c-0x28ccb8 control flow, one iteration = the 0x28c6e8 body + the advance
functions.semantics: Runs body(attachmentMap) once per attachment and reports which back edge the caller must take (ATTACHMENT is looped internally; SLOT / SKIN / DONE are returned). SKINS_GLUE_ERROR aborts without advancing. The slot head 0x28c6c4 and skin head 0x28c664 belong to other modules and are never re-entered here.

abi_notes: spAttachmentLoader_createAttachment is 5 arguments: r0 = json->loader, r1 = skin, r2 = requested type, r3 = name, [sp] = path (0x28c7a4/7a8/7ac/7b0/7b4). The recovered wrapper 0x284d58 frees and clears loader->error1/error2 before the vtable call.
spSkin_addAttachment: r0 = skin, r1 = slotIndex, r2 = name, r3 = attachment (0x28cc68..0x28cc78).
_spSkeletonJson_setError is 4 arguments (json, root, fmt, arg); the root is disposed inside it when non-NULL.
the jump table base is the addls instruction + 8 = 0x28c7d0 (ARM pc = addr + 8).

handoffs.to: one of the five type stub entries, with r7 = attachmentMap->name as the skin entry name
c/spine_read_region 0x28cdac / c/spine_read_bbox_path 0x28cd6c and 0x28ca5c / c/spine_read_mesh 0x28cb20 for the field parse
the caller's slot head 0x28c6c4 / skin head 0x28c664 on a non-ATTACHMENT advance
readSkeletonData_ikSection / transformSection / pathSection which report error_which == 2

open: the three "Target ..." tails cannot be executed with their original register value: r4 = r0 = 0, so [r4+0x1c] is a NULL-page read. The fixture injects an argument record to prove the offset and the register source; a total assembly that calls them with a real failed pointer would fault, exactly like the original.
the four field parsers are synthetic recorders in this module's fixture; their real bodies live in c/spine_read_region, c/spine_read_bbox_path and c/spine_read_mesh and are exercised by those modules
the Atlas loader body 0x284a08 is another module's scope; the fixture's loader record is a recorder that mirrors _spAttachmentLoader_setError's error1/error2 publication
the skin entry name comes from r7 (the JSON member key) while createAttachment receives the "name" property; the total assembly must reproduce that split, which is tested here through the loop driver
0x28bdcc / 0x28bdd8 / 0x28cc9c / 0x28ccb4 (common epilogue and chain-level restores) are deliberately not re-emitted
